executor_vs_analytic_verification.kind: VERIFICATION TARGET (can falsify the model; cannot establish the proof)
executor_vs_analytic_verification.reading: the analytic map reproduces the executor exactly (0.0) on the sampled domain; the FLOOR is enforced by max() and is therefore exact in the executor, because max returns one of its arguments. The NAIVE endpoint candidate that omits the inner clamp, max(T0, phi(dt)+delta_door), is NOT an upper bound and was exceeded by up to the recorded amount -- which is exactly why the errata corrected it to max(T0, max(target, phi(dt)) + delta_door); that corrected candidate was never exceeded. Both facts are recorded.

purpose: freeze the applicability domain of the continuous-time temperature proof and record the executor correspondence evidence. NOT the proof itself.

reachability_theorem_inputs.hard_bound_safety_iff: target_z > hard_low_z AND target_z + delta_door_z <= hard_high_z
reachability_theorem_inputs.statement: with every zone active, the only mechanism that can RAISE a zone above its target is that zone's own door event, and it adds exactly delta_door; hence the reachable set is [target_z, target_z + delta_door_z] per zone

state_mutation_corpus.conclusion: a dispatched vehicle trajectory is exactly: T := target at dispatch, then a sequence of transition_segment calls; no other code path mutates it

writes_to_compartment_temperature_c.role: dispatch_vehicle -> the VALID INITIAL STATE premise

admissible_band.analytic_threshold_reading: delta_z / margin_z: the worst-case excursion is driven back to the floor within this many hours (<= 3.4 minutes in every zone), so any segment at least this long ends EXACTLY at the floor and the map is constant
admissible_band.band: T0 in [target, target + delta_door] -- the band the theorem proves reachable
admissible_band.sampling: log-uniform sub-intervals, because uniform sampling almost never enters the only regime where segmentation can matter

sub_segment_composition.consequence: the executor applies its closed form ONCE per segment, so it is NOT a time discretisation of dT/dt = h(A-T) - c and splitting a segment does not give the same state (the gap grows with distance from the target). A continuous-time claim must therefore DECLARE its interpolation profile and its band. Inside the band this theorem proves REACHABLE, both gaps are recorded above; the proven statements themselves are about SEGMENT-BOUNDARY states, with the mid-segment profile a declared interpolation that coincides with the executor at every segment boundary.

unrestricted_band.band: T0 anywhere in [target, target+20] -- deliberately outside the reachable set
